evidence: Brief demands substantial real build work. instruction.md:1 asks for a multi-user recruiting workspace where 'the hard part is that nobody's work gets trampled'; :3 per-job pipeline board, one-stage moves with non-drag controls, shared manual order, interview capacity, refused-move rollback naming the colleague, all-or-none multi-card moves and undo; :5 live updates within 15 s preserving open card/note/cursor; :7 paginated long conversations with scroll anchoring, per-person unread, seen marks, per-user per-conversation drafts surviving sign-out; :9 candidate portal with data isolation; :13-15 Node/Express/SQLite server, DB_PATH, seed once, persistence across restarts. hireops_rules.md sections 1-9 add role matrix (401/403/404), version-based 409 conflicts, activity log, undo semantics. Smallest submission satisfying the brief is therefore a full stateful multi-role server-backed SPA with polling/SSE; a static page, single CRUD screen or mock does not satisfy it. Grading enforces this: both gates are zero-weight all_pass gates (scoring.toml [gates]; score.py:126-133 gives reward 0 if a gate fails). gates/render/judge.toml criterion hro_gate_render requires a wrong-password refusal plus real sign-in to a usable staff workspace ('A static picture or only a health response is insufficient'); gates/constraints/judge.toml hro_gate_shared requires UI-created job + candidate visible to the Observer in an independent browser context ('A static seed response, a no-op success message, a browser-only save or a job-only app does not satisfy the gate'). Each scored prompt repeats this minimal backend check and zeroes every row on a static shell. Stub ceiling, computed from tests/scored/functional/judge.toml: a gate-passing CRUD-only app (auth + job/candidate CRUD with validation, 401s, seed + persistence) could at most earn hro_job_open 0.5 + hro_add_candidate 0.5 + hro_add_email_rules 1 + hro_anonymous 1.5 + hro_restart 1.5 = 5.0 of 58.5 = 0.085 functional (just above the 0.05 floor, which is byte-identical to the template scoring.toml, so not task-controlled); all five polish rows (live board/thread preservation, scroll anchoring, failed send, session resume) need the hard features, so polish ~0; visual Likert at best ~0.5-0.75 normalized. Reward ceiling ~0.6*0.085 + 0.2*0 + 0.2*0.75 = ~0.20 versus a full build near 1.0; the remaining 53.5 functional weight (stale 409, bulk, undo, live board, threads, unread, seen, drafts, candidate privacy) requires real work. A 'trivial tweak' is impossible: no starter app is shipped (template solution/app/server.js is a placeholder; agent environment ships only assets and instructions). Conforming alternative check: the brief leaves routes, labels, layout and transport (polling/SSE/sockets) open (hireops_rules.md:3-5, :123; app_context.md 'The app may use any route layout and labels'), so a differently-structured real build is not excluded for this row. Golden is a real implementation (src/index.js 450 lines, board.js 373, threads.js 223); scripted golden observations in qc/repairs/hireops-2026-10-03-workspace/results/workspace.json (hash verified) show 25 groups passing, but that is a scripted run, not a configured judge run. Risk=true because raw-evidence-index.json scope states 'Full configured grading/workload, reward discrimination/ranking and Oracle/target scores are absent': no measured stub/weak-app reward exists to confirm the ~0.20 ceiling estimate or that the judge actually zeroes a static shell. The nonzero partial reward a gate-passing CRUD stub can collect is a Note under the template's shaped reward, not a defect of this row.
counterexample: Plausible broken app tried on paper: a styled single-page CRUD app with real login, SQLite job/candidate create, email validation, 401 on anonymous calls and seed persistence, but no moves rules, conflicts, live updates, conversations or candidate portal. It passes both gates and could earn about 0.20 reward (functional 5/58.5 above the template 0.05 floor plus visual craft) but cannot approach full reward; not a Fail for this row, unmeasured.
suggested_fix: None required for this row; before clearance, record a measured weak-app/stub run (reward discrimination evidence) to confirm the stub ceiling, without altering the template floor or shared scoring policy.
